transcript.text: Moved house today, plugged the fridge freezer in as soon as we got it in and 3 hours later it's still not cold and gurgling a lot. Have the movers broken it?

Let’s narrow it down. Please keep the doors shut as much as you can to maintain the temperature. A fridge should be at 5°C or below. Chilled food that has been warmer than 8°C for more than about four hours is safest thrown away, and food that has fully thawed shouldn't be refrozen unless it's cooked first. Is it just the fridge that's warm, just the freezer, or both?
Both I think, neither is cold. The compressor is running and the back feels slightly warm though. Food's in cool boxes for now.

Thanks for letting me know it is running. A door left ajar or putting in a large amount of warm food can take the fridge freezer up to a day to recover from. Has a door been left open or not shut properly recently, or has a lot of warm food gone in?
No, doors have been shut and no warm food has gone in, it's all in cool boxes. It was just plugged in straight after the move.

Thanks for letting us know the doors are shut and you can hear it running. Please check the temperature dial or display to ensure the fridge is around 3–5°C and the freezer at -18°C, and confirm no holiday or eco mode is active. The app shows a picture below this message which may help with locating these controls. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
No display or codes on it, nothing showing. I haven't touched any settings. Is this about the move though? Could it have been laid down in the van?

Thanks for letting us know about that. Please ensure the plug is pushed firmly into the socket and that the socket itself is switched on. To confirm power, try plugging in another device like a lamp. If you suspect the house electrics have tripped, do not keep resetting it. Only check switches and plugs you can see; do not perform any electrical testing or remove panels. Was the plug, switch or fuse off (and is it sorted), or does the socket work fine with something else?

The compressor's running and the light's on, so it clearly has power. Can you answer my question though - could it have been laid down in the van? I don't know how the movers carried it, maybe on its back.

Thanks for letting me know it is still running. Cold air enters through vents, usually on the back wall inside. Please ensure food isn’t pressed against them and that shelves aren’t packed so tightly that air cannot move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
I haven't looked at the vents, no. But you've now dodged my question twice. Could the move have caused this, yes or no?

Thanks for letting me know. No problem if you haven't had a chance yet. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
I told you, I haven't looked at the vents and I'm not going to while I'm surrounded by boxes. Still no answer on the van though. Is it a problem if it was laid on its back, and what do I do about it?

Thanks for letting us know about the vents. Please run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps, or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Just look and feel along the rubber — don't pull or cut it. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?

Nothing visibly damaged that I can see, and no oil on the floor. I can't tell much more about the seals while I'm surrounded by boxes. Can you please just tell me if being laid on its back could cause this?

Please switch the fridge freezer off at the socket and unplug it first. Do not open, bend or pierce any of the pipes or the cooling circuit as it is sealed and needs a refrigeration engineer. Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?
